title: Pharmacological mechanisms and therapeutic potential of Puerarin in post-stroke rehabilitation: Insights from network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Li, Lei; Zhou, Chunxiang; Sun, Ying
one_liner_zh: 该文研究葛根素通过HIF-1α/VEGF通路促进卒中后血管再生的药理机制，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of disability, and promoting post-stroke recovery through endothelial regeneration and angiogenesis is crucial for improving patient outcomes. Puerarin, a flavonoid derived from Pueraria lobata, has shown promise in enhancing angiogenesis and endothelial function. This study investigates the pharmacological mechanisms of Puerarin in post-stroke rehabilitation through network pharmacology and experimental validation. METHODS: Network pharmacology was used to identify potential gene targets of Puerarin and their association with post-stroke sequelae. A Venn diagram analysis identified 116 common targets. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analyses were performed to identify enriched pathways. Molecular docking simulations were used to confirm interactions between Puerarin and key targets. Additionally, in vitro experiments using human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/re-oxygenation (OGD/R) were conducted to assess Puerarin's effects on cell migration, proliferation, and angiogenesis. RESULTS: Network pharmacology revealed several key pathways, with the HIF-1alpha/VEGF signaling pathway identified as a critical target. Experimental validation confirmed that Puerarin enhanced endothelial cell migration, proliferation, and angiogenesis in a concentration-dependent manner. At lower concentrations, Puerarin promoted angiogenesis and endothelial migration. Molecular docking simulations demonstrated favorable binding interactions between Puerarin and key angiogenic targets. CONCLUSIONS: Puerarin may serve as a therapeutic agent for post-stroke rehabilitation, promoting vascular regeneration through endothelial cell migration and angiogenesis. Its ability to activate the HIF-1alpha/VEGF pathway underscores its potential in improving functional recovery. Further in vivo studies are required to optimize dosing, assess long-term efficacy, and explore clinical applications.
abstract_zh: 背景：卒中（stroke）是导致残疾的主要原因，通过内皮再生和血管生成（angiogenesis）促进卒中后恢复对改善患者预后至关重要。葛根素（Puerarin）是从葛根（Pueraria lobata）中提取的一种黄酮类化合物，在增强血管生成和内皮功能方面显示出潜力。本研究通过网络药理学和实验验证，探讨葛根素在卒中后康复中的药理学机制。方法：采用网络药理学方法鉴定葛根素的潜在基因靶点及其与卒中后遗症的相关性。维恩图分析确定了116个共同靶点。进行基因本体论（Gene Ontology, GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, KEGG）通路分析以识别富集通路。分子对接模拟用于确认葛根素与关键靶点之间的相互作用。此外，使用暴露于氧糖剥夺/再氧合（oxygen-glucose deprivation/re-oxygenation, OGD/R）的人脐静脉内皮细胞（human umbilical vein endothelial cells, HUVECs）进行体外实验，评估葛根素对细胞迁移、增殖和血管生成的影响。结果：网络药理学揭示了若干关键通路，其中HIF-1alpha/VEGF信号通路被确定为关键靶点。实验验证确认，葛根素以浓度依赖性方式增强内皮细胞迁移、增殖和血管生成。在较低浓度下，葛根素促进血管生成和内皮迁移。分子对接模拟显示葛根素与关键血管生成靶点之间存在良好的结合相互作用。结论：葛根素可能作为卒中后康复的治疗药物，通过内皮细胞迁移和血管生成促进血管再生。其激活HIF-1alpha/VEGF通路的能力凸显了其在改善功能恢复方面的潜力。需要进一步的体内研究以优化剂量、评估长期疗效并探索临床应用。
